title: What If Mount Pinatubo Erupted Again?

scenes.text: What if Pinatubo erupted again? The first change wouldn't be the ground. It'd be the sky.
In 1991, its ash cloud climbed about twelve miles, or twenty kilometers, straight up.
It also pumped twenty million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, the largest cloud of it ever observed.
That made the biggest aerosol layer in the stratosphere of the twentieth century.
The result: Earth's surface cooled by about half a degree Celsius for two to four years.
One volcano cooled the whole planet's surface, and warmed the sky above it by up to three and a half degrees.
